newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Three hurt as Honduras police dislodge protesters.
newsitem.headline: Three hurt as Honduras police dislodge protesters.

text.p: Three people were injured on Monday when Honduran army troops and police forcibly broke up a protest by some 4,000 native Indians in front of the presidential palace, officials said.
An Indian woman and a child were hurt as well as one police official when scuffles broke out between security forces and protesters, police and Indian leaders said.
"The military and police dislodged our protest violently and a woman and a boy were beaten up in the process," Salvador Zuniga, a leader of the Chortis Indians, told Reuters.

The Chortis Indians, descendants of the Maya, had staged a week-long sit-in blocking the gates to the presidential palace to demand both lands in eastern Honduras and an investigation into the recent murders of two Indian leaders.
Army troops and riot police swooped in on the protesters at 4:30 a.m. local time (10:30 GMT) after talks between the group and government officials broke down late on Sunday.
After the protest was broken up, the group threatened to call a hunger strike. They reassembled early on Monday on a soccer field about half a mile (one kilometre) from the presidential palace.
